title: The AI That Lied
briefing_md:
Kiranaa Mart is a fictional grocery chain with 120 stores in four regions.

Every Monday at 6:00 AM an AI assistant, InsightBot, writes the weekly sales report for management. This Monday (20 October) it reported that North region revenue had crashed by 61% and recommended a closure review for nine North stores. The CEO forwarded it to the board at 9:10 AM.

The North store managers say their weekend was normal. The analytics team says the new AI model is hallucinating.

Find out where the wrong numbers really came from: the model, the prompt, the data, the API or a person.
root_cause_options: Human error during an approved change
Bad or wrongly formatted input data
Test or staging activity hitting production
twist_md: The IT team has dug out an email from the POS (billing software) vendor that was sitting unread in a shared mailbox.

content.prompt: Write the weekly performance report for leadership using the attached regional sales table.
content.output:
WEEKLY PERFORMANCE — 13–19 Oct

North: ₹0.38 Cr (−61% week on week). Nine stores (N-02, N-04, N-05, N-07, N-08, N-11, N-12, N-14, N-15) show revenue below ₹5,000 for the week.
South: ₹3.12 Cr (+2%). East: ₹2.41 Cr (+1%). West: ₹2.87 Cr (−1%).

Recommendation: start a closure review for the nine underperforming North stores immediately.

content.subject: BillEase 5.2 rolling out tonight to pilot stores
content.body_md:
BillEase 5.2 will auto-install on Sunday 19 Oct at 23:00 for your pilot group (North region, 9 stores).

What's new: regional number formatting. CSV exports now use the store locale by default, e.g. 1.234,56 (dot for thousands, comma for decimals). To keep the old format, set export.locale=en-IN before the update.

answer.root_cause_md: Before the twist, the Friday model upgrade (E02), the 'be decisive' prompt change (E03) and the analytics chat (E04) point at the AI. Careful teams see that rolling back changed nothing (E04), that the model only repeats the totals it is given (E09, E11), and that the raw CSV uses a comma as the decimal separator (E08) which the parser strips (E06).
answer.post_twist_category: Bad or wrongly formatted input data
answer.post_twist_responsible: BillEase POS 5.2 switched the nine North pilot stores' CSV exports to the 1.234,56 number format; etl/parse_pos.py strips commas, so every amount became about 1/1000th of its real value; the data-quality alert fired but its channel was muted. The AI reported its input faithfully.
